title: Redwood POC scoping with Bluecrest Health - security pilot
summary: POC scoping focused on security and compliance requirements for a pilot: SOC 2 / ISO evidence, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC model, audit log retention and access controls. Discussed workload sizing for inference benchmarks, success criteria (latency, throughput, accuracy), timeline (6-8 week pilot), and next steps to share docs and schedule bench runs.
next_steps: Redwood to send SOC 2 Type II and ISO attestation links
SE to share SAML SSO integration guide and example metadata.xml
Schedule initial benchmark week (3 days) w/ sample dataset - suggested week of Sep 18
Draft pilot statement of work and success criteria doc
Customer to provide redacted sample workload and target SLAs
action_items: Lena Park: send SOC2/ISO docs and security pack by 2028-09-05
Marcus Chen: share SAML metadata and RBAC model example by 2028-09-06
Sara Morgan: circulate redacted sample dataset and baseline latency requirements by 2028-09-08
Kevin Lowe: confirm QA test accounts and data retention needs by 2028-09-09
transcript:
[00:00] Lena Park: ok everyone, thanks for joining. this is lena from Redwood, i'm the AE on this. we got marcus and priya on the line from our engineering team. can you do quick intros?
[00:08] Dr. Angela Ruiz: sure, angela ruiz, ciso at bluecrest. we run a mix of cloud and on-prem systems, lots of PHI, so security's the top req.
[00:15] Tom Ellis: tom, director of eng, i'll own the integration side.
[00:20] Sara Morgan: sara, cloud architect, i'll share infra constraints.
[00:25] Marcus Chen: hey all, marcus, solutions eng at redwood - i'll lead the benchmarks and deployment plan.
[00:30] Lena Park: thanks. quick agenda: scope pilot success criteria, sizing/benchmarks, security/compliance checklist (SOC2, ISO, sso), and timeline.
[00:38] Dr. Angela Ruiz: sounds good. our main question up front - can the pilot run with no PHI leaving our VPC? we need private deployment or an isolated env.
[00:45] Marcus Chen: yes. we offer Redwood Private (sometimes called redwood privet in older notes - sorry, transcript quirk) which can be deployed into a customer VPC or on-prem. we can run the pilot inside your environment and integrate with your KMS for key management.
[00:58] Sara Morgan: what KMS do you support? we use AWS KMS and a corporate HSM for certain keys.
[01:04] Marcus Chen: AWS KMS is supported, and we have integrations for external HSMs via KMIP in our private package. we'll include relevant config samples.
[01:12] Tom Ellis: audit logs - we need immutable audit trails for requests, who invoked, model version, and redaction flags. retention policy 1 year minimum, but for some processes we might need 3 years.
[01:22] Marcus Chen: default audit logs come through our audit pipeline; retention is configurable. for private deployments we can ship logs to your splunk or s3 bucket with timestamped, signed entries. we'll note immutability options and also include checksum metadata.
[01:33] Dr. Angela Ruiz: SOC 2 and ISO - can you provide your reports? also do you have pen test results?
[01:38] Lena Park: yes, we'll share SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 attestation links. pen test summary is available in the security pack; full reports under NDA. i'll email those after the call.
[01:46] Sara Morgan: and SSO - we use Okta and Ping, SAML only, no OIDC for now.
[01:51] Marcus Chen: we support SAML SSO and SSO for the console. for API keys and service accounts we support RBAC and can integrate with SCIM for user provisioning. i'll send example metadata.xml and an Okta setup guide.
[02:02] Kevin Lowe: RBAC granularity - can we restrict read/write to model endpoints per team, and restrict who can rollout model versions?
[02:08] Priya Singh: yes we have role types: admin, infra, developer, read-only, and you can customize roles. model rollout permission is a separate privilege - we'll show the RBAC matrix in the pilot doc.
[02:18] Tom Ellis: good. now on benchmarks - we need to validate latency and throughput. target is P95 latency under 250ms for single-turn prompts at 2k token context and sustained throughput of ~50 reqs/sec for our busiest routes.
[02:32] Marcus Chen: ok that's helpful. for a preliminary run we recommend: 3-day benchmark, mixture of 70% gen prompts, 20% embeddings, 10% rerank. we'll instrument token-level latency and tail latencies. we can run on Dedicated GPUs or in your private infra depending on isolation needs.
[02:47] Lena Park: question for bluecrest - are you okay with a small subset of redacted production queries for the benchmark? we just need realistic distribution.
[02:54] Sara Morgan: yes, redacted is fine, as long as the redaction rules remove PHI.
[02:58] Marcus Chen: perfect. for cost-sensitivity, we can provide quantized model variants to reduce GPU memory and token cost; we'll show cost/perf tradeoffs in the benchmark spreadsheet.
[03:08] Dr. Angela Ruiz: also want to confirm data at rest encryption and KMS key rotation policies - we rotate keys quarterly.
[03:14] Marcus Chen: supported. key rotation via AWS KMS automated rotation works; for HSM we can coordinate manual rotations. logs will show key id used for each encryption event.
[03:22] Tom Ellis: who on the redwood side is our contact for security review? we sometimes need live Q&A with security folks.
[03:27] Lena Park: i'll be primary owner; i'll loop in our head of security, Raj Patel, for a 1:1 security review. expect a follow-up meeting if needed.
[03:35] Kevin Lowe: success criteria - let's be explicit: 1) P95 latency <=250ms on target workload; 2) throughput >=50 rps sustained; 3) no PHI leaves our VPC; 4) audit logs available and queryable for 12 months; 5) RBAC enforced and SSO integrated.
[03:50] Marcus Chen: that matches what we've heard. we'll draft a success criteria doc and add pass/fail thresholds. for accuracy / quality, do you have automated evals or human review thresholds?
[03:59] Tom Ellis: QA will run labeled evals. we need a human-in-the-loop check for critical responses. goal is <3% critical error rate on sampled outputs.
[04:08] Marcus Chen: noted. on timelines - pilot kickoff: 2028-09-18 (week of) preferred, with a 6 week churn: week 1-2 infra & SSO setup, week 3-4 bench runs, week 5 analysis, week 6 wrap + decision. is that realistic?
[04:23] Sara Morgan: yes, works for our timeline provided you can deliver the SOC docs and SAML guide before kickoff.
[04:29] Lena Park: we'll send docs by Monday Sep 5. SE to schedule an infra sync with sara for Sep 7 or 8.
[04:36] Marcus Chen: i'll propose two time slots after the call. also we'll set up a small staging cluster in your VPC for the bench runs.
[04:42] Dr. Angela Ruiz: pen test - if you need our team to run a targeted assessment, we can coordinate. otherwise we'll rely on your pen test summary.
[04:49] Marcus Chen: if you can run a short acceptance test from your scanner against the staging cluster that would be helpful; we'll provide a whitelist and test plan.
[04:57] Tom Ellis: ok. any blockers we haven't discussed? compliance of logs with our audit team and data residency.
[05:04] Priya Singh: for residency, private deployment in region is doable; we'll confirm supported regions in the security pack.
[05:10] Lena Park: recap / next steps: i) send SOC2/ISO/pen-test summary and security pack; ii) marcus send SAML/SCIM docs and RBAC matrix; iii) sara to provide redacted sample dataset and latency baselines; iv) schedule infra sync and bench week.
[05:24] Dr. Angela Ruiz: sounds good. thank you.
[05:27] Lena Park: thanks all - we'll follow up with calendar invites and docs.
[05:30] [call ends]

Notes: transcript has occasional mis-attribution and auto-caption errors (K M S vs KMS, redwood privet/priv**e**t for private), see attached: Security Pack link (shared post-call) https://redwood.example.com/security-pack, SAML guide: https://redwood.example.com/saml-setup, benchmark spreadsheet: https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/bch-sample.
